dialogues.speaker: Basima the Fifth
dialogues.text: A-hmm-hmm-hmm~ Now you've played Bing-Bang Finchball, have you not? The cute Finch family has a new member, the Ancient Scarlet-Plume Finch! Pretty amazing, right?

response.speaker: Basima the Fifth
response.text: Looks like you're enjoying the little finch's hopping around, too!

choices.text: Doesn't the ball hurt the finch?

response.speaker: Basima the Fifth
response.text: What a thoughtful worry! I felt the same way when I first saw it. You see, the bouncing ball really does stay close to the little finch, so anyone with a kind heart might fret a bit.

response.speaker: Basima the Fifth
response.text: But let me tell you a story. When I first arrived in Atocpan, I accidentally provoked a brown deer by the lingering scent of spices on me, and it began chasing me.

response.speaker: Basima the Fifth
response.text: Then, out of nowhere, this little finch hopped out from the roadside, nudged the deer, and seemed to settle things with it...

response.speaker: Basima the Fifth
response.text: And just like that, my worries disappeared.

response.speaker: Basima the Fifth
response.text: That's right! I was very much surprised. Worried that this little finch might have been hurt, I tried to make friends with it and even took it to see a vet...

response.speaker: Basima the Fifth
response.text: The check-up showed it was perfectly fine. What an adorable and resilient little cutie!

response.speaker: Basima the Fifth
response.text: It made me realize... maybe I've been thinking too rigidly.

response.speaker: Basima the Fifth
response.text: I'd always equated "cuteness" with "being delicate," thinking that anything cute needs careful protection — even to the point of restricting it...

response.speaker: Basima the Fifth
response.text: But true cuteness can lie in a being that is both powerful and gentle.

response.speaker: Basima the Fifth
response.text: Hehe, I knew you'd see it the same way!

response.speaker: Basima the Fifth
response.text: All in all, this little finch has inspired me to discover a whole new way to appreciate the cuteness of finches!

response.speaker: Basima the Fifth
response.text: After returning to the Atocpan from Nod-Krai, the first thing I did was meet up with my finch friend!

choices.text: I can think of so many examples now.
Looks like the game development is going smoothly.

response.speaker: Basima the Fifth
response.text: Yes! Thanks to the generous benefactor I met in Nod-Krai, who provided substantial funding, the new Finch Ball's effects are much more dynamic and lively!

response.speaker: Basima the Fifth
response.text: All my benefactor asked for were a few of the new Finchballs and permission for some moderate adaptations, not even a share of the profits... How incredibly generous!

response.speaker: Basima the Fifth
response.text: However, there's still one goal I haven't achieved.

response.speaker: Basima the Fifth
response.text: Originally, activating the "Double Trouble!" Bouncing Finchball was supposed to summon two finch partners to help fight off those gulls...

response.speaker: Basima the Fifth
response.text: But the artisan crafting the balls said she's completely swamped with orders and asked for a two-week delay.

response.speaker: Basima the Fifth
response.text: So for now, I'm just substituting it with the current Finchball. Once the other little finch type is ready, we'll roll out the updated version!

choices.text: Oh, wow! So we can expect even more visual effects?

response.speaker: Basima the Fifth
response.text: Keep both? What do you mean?

choices.text: One version features different finches teaming up...

response.speaker: Basima the Fifth
response.text: Hmm, that actually makes sense! This way we could even cater to different preferences. What a brilliant solution!

response.speaker: Basima the Fifth
response.text: If I ever get to work with you again, I hope you would let me recommend my Finchballs to visitors and fellow workers — as long as it doesn't get in the way of your own business, of course.

response.speaker: Basima the Fifth
response.text: I'm sure they'd lift everyone's spirits and bring so much joy!

choices.text: Another version features a trio... we could call them the "Finchy Tri-Stars."
Could we actually keep both versions?
I'll be back later to see the finches~

response.speaker: Basima the Fifth
response.text: Please do! It's so much more fun when you can play without a care.
